key_insight: OSCAR routes optimization-modeling tasks across LLMs and uses a certified simulator to keep searching until it finds not just a feasible solution, but a verified improvement over prior candidates.
engineering_relevance: This gives organizations a practical way to build lower-cost, locally deployable LLM-based optimization pipelines that respect labeled operating rules and adaptively trade off price, capability, and stopping time.
method: Use an offline certified Simulator to compare candidate formulations against labeled feasible/infeasible decision examples.
Run a Coder/Reviewer loop and escalate from cheaper to stronger LLMs when needed.
Formulate model selection and stopping as sequential decision-making under uncertainty, with cost-ordered escalation and a prior-free guarantee.
evidence_signal: On five benchmark problems, OSCAR reached 95%–100% accuracy with two small open-weight models, and in five runs per problem its token costs were on average 3.1× and 5.8× lower than Codex and Claude Code.
watch_item: Performance depends on having reliable labeled decision examples and a certified simulator; if those labels are incomplete or inconsistent, the framework may reinforce incorrect operating rules.
paper_title: OR for AI That Does OR: Routing LLMs up the Escalator inside the OSCAR Framework
